usageNotes: Use this to audit or display the ordered cluster-level firewall ruleset for a PVE remote managed by PDM. Rules are returned in positional order (pos field); the effective policy is applied top-down, so position matters when reasoning about overlapping rules. Requires Resource.Audit on the target remote — read-only tokens are sufficient.

examples.summary: List all cluster firewall rules for the 'prod-pve' remote

tips: The 'pos' field is the rule's index in the ordered ruleset — lower pos values are evaluated first.
Rules with 'enable' set to 0 (or omitted as falsy) are inactive; check this field before assuming a rule is enforced.
The 'action' field can be ACCEPT, DROP, REJECT, or a security group name — security group references expand to their member rules at evaluation time.
Cluster-level rules apply to all nodes in the remote; for per-VM or per-node rules use the appropriate guest/host firewall endpoints instead.
